Below is a concise list of the **countries that have historically won the most Olympic gold medals (Summer + Winter combined, up to the most recent Games in 2024)** together with the **capital city of each nation**.  

| Rank* | Country (IOC code) | Approx. total gold medals won* | Capital city |
|------|--------------------|--------------------------------|--------------|
| 1 | United States (USA) | ~2 900 gold medals | Washington, D.C. |
| 2 | Soviet Union (URS) † | ~1 010 gold medals | Moscow |
| 3 | Great Britain (GBR) | ~  900 gold medals | London |
| 4 | Germany (GER) | ~  860 gold medals | Berlin |
| 5 | France (FRA) | ~  840 gold medals | Paris |
| 6 | Italy (ITA) | ~  770 gold medals | Rome |
| 7 | China (CHN) | ~  660 gold medals | Beijing |
| 8 | Sweden (SWE) | ~  640 gold medals | Stockholm |
| 9 | Australia (AUS) | ~  620 gold medals | Canberra |
| 10| Japan (JPN) | ~  550 gold medals | Tokyo |

\* **Rank** is based on the cumulative number of gold medals earned at **all Summer and Winter Olympic Games** up to and including the **2024 Paris Summer Olympics** (the most recent data available from the International Olympic Committee’s official medal database).  

† The Soviet Union dissolved in 1991; its former capital was **Moscow**, which is now the capital of the Russian Federation. The medal total listed includes the medals earned by the USSR (including those of the 1992 “Unified Team”).

### Quick notes

* The United States has a decisive lead, largely thanks to its long‑standing dominance in both Summer and Winter sports.  
* The Soviet Union, although no longer a country, still ranks second because its historic medal haul (1952‑1988) was enormous.  
* Great Britain’s high rank reflects its status as the host of the modern Games (1908, 1948, 2012) and a consistently strong performer, especially in recent decades.  
* Germany’s total combines medals earned by West Germany (FRG), East Germany (GDR) and the reunified Germany after 1990.  
* China’s rapid ascent in the last three‑four decades has moved it into the top‑ten list, highlighted by record‑breaking performances at the 2008 Beijing, 2012 London, 2016 Rio, 2020 Tokyo (held 2021) and 2024 Paris Games.  

If you need a more detailed breakdown (e.g., separate Summer vs. Winter totals, or a longer list), just let me know!
